A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiSK and contain the main paper and Appendices A-C. Their text, equations, figures, and tables are readable and support reliable matching despite pagination and reporting changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original synthetic regression experiments, image classification training, and language-model fine-tuning results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain original experimental outcomes across synthetic, vision, and language tasks, including comparisons and hyperparameter ablations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 3 retains the same two-point gradient combination, clipping and noise injection, fixed-gain filtering, and base-optimizer update. The rewritten Kalman correction is algebraically equivalent; explanatory and implementation-interface edits do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic regression, MNIST, CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet-1k, the same four GLUE tasks, E2E, and DART. Training-from-scratch and fine-tuning coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain DP-SGD, DPAdam/AdamW, DPLoRA, DOPPLER, DP-FTRL, and the same cited SOTA methods. The rerun De et al. ImageNet baseline was already reported in v1 Appendix C.3; its use in revised summaries does not introduce a comparator.

E3.justification: Table 6 changes the reported ImageNet-1k model from ViT to ResNet-50, a revision to the stated experimental configuration. The PDFs do not establish that this experiment was rerun. Newly specified sampling and tuning procedures are disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to existing protocols.

E4.justification: The hyperparameter sensitivity heatmaps in Figure 8, synthetic noise-level comparison in Figure 6a, and supplementary training comparisons are retained. The new explanation of two-point averaging interprets existing evidence without adding an ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. Theoretical noise variances and covariance calculations are not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 6 replaces the ImageNet pair 40.00/36.35 with 36.89/33.56; Appendix C.3 in both versions identifies these as validation and test pairs, respectively. Section 5.2 also changes 36.4/32.4 to 36.89/33.56. These revise reported summaries without establishing a new same-setting performance gain; other performance tables and underlying curves are retained.

T1.justification: Corollary 1 adds explicit lower bounds on batch size and iteration count and revises the step-size prescription and bound's noise dependence. Theorem 3 changes its iteration horizon and privacy-utility expression and requires sufficiently large N. Appendix B adds bounded-gradient and clipping conditions to Lemma 1 and corrects algebraic steps. These substantively revise the guarantees beyond notation changes.

C1.justification: The contributions now qualify the theoretical improvement factor as problem-dependent and describe empirical comparisons under the same or tighter privacy budgets. The headline ImageNet comparison uses the 33.56% baseline instead of 32.4%. The central claims about DiSK's denoising framework and improved DP training remain.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly interprets the existing DOPPLER comparisons as suggesting that averaging gradients at two points before clipping may be particularly important. Section 4.1 also describes the theoretical benefit more precisely as an improvement in an iteration-complexity upper bound rather than directly in convergence rate.

D1.justification: V2 documents the Opacus/FastDP RDP accountant, fixed-size sampling without replacement, and test-set-based hyperparameter selection. Table 7 supplies dataset-specific privacy parameters and comparator values. It also adds an Opacus implementation link and revises the optimizer-wrapper example while retaining the anonymous experiment-code link.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wang, Balle, and Kasiviswanathan (2019) to support privacy accounting and cites Kalman (1960) more prominently in the main text, although that work already appeared in v1. The related-work scope and principal positioning against earlier optimization and filtering methods remain stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording corrections and expands explanations of filtering and proof steps. It updates author affiliations and publication headers and adds acknowledgements. The section hierarchy and overall narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 7 and fits Table 6 onto one page. Figures 1 and 5 receive clearer improvement labels and captions; their green improvement curves already existed in v1. Figure 6b removes the redundant improvement curve and secondary axis while retaining all method curves. Other changes mainly concern placement and spacing.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful precision and transparency gains through explicit theoretical conditions, proof corrections, reproducibility disclosures, and an ImageNet summary using test values already documented in v1. The improvement is limited: Section 5.2 still associates the revised ImageNet accuracy with ViT-small, whereas Table 6 specifies ResNet-50, leaving model attribution unclear.
